question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared `notificationWake.reactions` policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical reaction-triggered turn contract, or choose a narrower per-channel/per-message design instead?
rationale: This issue asks for new public wake/config semantics across messaging channels, and automation should not pick between the open shared and Discord-specific implementations without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Adopt Shared Policy
options.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off reaction policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best implementation with docs, metadata, tests, and live proof as needed.

options.title: Narrow The Contract
options.body: Start with a Discord-only, Telegram-only, or per-message await-reaction contract and explicitly accept a later unification pass.

options.title: Defer Reaction Wakes
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and pause or close the open implementation candidates until the product surface is clearer.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Policy
recommendation.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off reaction policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best implementation with docs, metadata, tests, and live proof as needed.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the open shared-policy candidate and has recent history across the reaction, config, and heartbeat-adjacent paths.
